entries.title: The watch and the town's defences
q: how do i defend my village
how do i keep monsters out
entries.answer: A town sees to its own safety. Guards (twice a folk's health) walk the watch; streets are lit with torches, then lamp posts; from the Stone Age a wall with gates shut at dusk, watch posts and an alarm bell; an Iron Age town keeps an iron golem. When trouble comes the bell rings, gates shut, guards man the walls and everyone else goes indoors.
tips: The elder orders 'Man the walls' after lives were lost or the bell rang.
Kill monsters near folk yourself and the town thanks you.

entries.title: Raids and the alarm bell
entries.answer: About one night in five a walled town of ten or more with a watch is raided: a band (zombies and a skeleton in the Stone Age, spiders joining in the Iron Age, pillagers and vindicators from the Diamond Age) comes at a gate after dark. The bell rings when four or more monsters get inside the wall or raiders are sighted; guards with bows shoot from the posts.
tips: Kill raiders and every folk thinks better of you; a raid night doubles the bounty.
There are no raids on Peaceful; an operator can turn them off in the config.

entries.title: Crime, the watch's cases and special constables
q: how do i arrest a folk
entries.answer: Now and then a poor or bitter folk pickpockets, steals, vandalises or forges coin. The watch (the constable from the Iron Age) investigates clues and witnesses, names a culprit, and the council holds court. Ask any folk 'Seen anything?' or 'Report a crime' (Town → The watch). A citizen or friend with a clean record can ask a guard 'Swear me in' to get a Constable's Badge.
steps: Talk → Town → The watch → Seen anything? / Report a crime.
To become a special constable: Town → The watch → Swear me in.
With the badge: right-click a culprit to arrest it; use the badge in the air to join or leave the beat.
controls: [Right-click] a folk with the Constable's Badge → arrest
tips: Footprints of mud lead from a scene until rain washes them out; a dropped keepsake names its owner.
A convicted folk may sit in the stocks on the square.

entries.title: Outlaws, bounties and prisoners of war
q: i am an outlaw what do i do
entries.answer: After a war towns hold prisoners (ask a guard 'Prisoners of war', buy a release, or get one out). Someone who does enough wrong is outlawed: a WANTED poster goes up and its guards take them on sight. Bring an outlaw in and claim the bounty from a guard. As an outlaw yourself, 'Give yourself up', or ask the elder for a pardon.
controls: [Right-click] a guard → Town → The watch → Outlaws wanted · Claim a bounty · A wanted poster
Town → The watch → Give yourself up · Ask for a pardon
tips: A guard writes you a Wanted Poster; or craft a blank one (paper, an ink sac and red dye) and use it in a town.

entries.title: War between towns
q: how do i end a war
entries.answer: Wars are rare and never for nothing: two feuding neighbours, a real grievance, a hawkish elder who likes the odds, and a council that votes aye. A herald brings an ultimatum; refused, both towns ring their bells and hang war banners. Armies muster, march and fight battles you can watch from the hill, and a war ends at the table with a treaty.
steps: Follow it on the town's books: Civic → War and War map.
Join your town's army when it musters (you're told in chat with a horn).
Or work for peace: carry peace terms, or ask folk to make peace.
controls: Town's books → Civic → War · War map
tips: War-weariness grows every day of a war: length, cost, a short larder, lost trade.
An operator can turn wars off; then a feud stays a feud.

entries.title: The war room's map table
q: what does the map table do
see a map of the region
where are the other towns on a map
how do i see armies on the map
entries.answer: Right-click a map table for the war room: a live map of the region as the town knows it, with towns' lands and borders, roads and trade routes, armies on the march, camps, battles, sieges, caravans, envoys, scouts, ruins, harbours and wonders. Drag to pan, scroll (or + and −) to zoom, click a town for its card.
controls: Drag pan · [Scroll] or [+][−] zoom · click a town
tips: Craft it from 2 paper, a compass, 2 planks, a cartography table and 2 sticks.
Unknown land is left the colour of the paper.

entries.title: Neighbours, feuds and making peace
q: how do i make peace between towns
entries.answer: Every pair of neighbouring towns has a relationship: allies, friendly, wary, a feud, war. Ask a folk 'Neighbours' (World tab) to hear how they stand. Say 'make peace with Kingsgate' to urge peace in a feud, or (if you must) stir up trouble. Envoys travel between towns with offers of trade, alliances and the business of war.

entries.title: Weapons and armour: steel, pikes, halberds, bows
q: what weapons does the mod add
entries.answer: Steel (an iron ingot and any coal, or blast an iron ingot) sits between iron and diamond: steel sword, helmet, chestplate, leggings and boots. Military research adds the pike (more reach, hard on riders), halberd (reach and a steel edge), war hammer (slow but through armour), longbow (faster, harder arrows) and arbalest (a steel-strung crossbow).
tips: Recipes: pike (iron ingot, 2 sticks), halberd (2 steel, 2 sticks), war hammer (3 iron, 2 sticks), longbow (4 sticks, 3 string), arbalest (2 iron, a steel ingot, a crossbow); steel armour like iron armour in steel.
Towns muster pikes and halberds into the line and win the archers' duel with longbows and arbalests.

entries.title: A town on a war footing, scouts and spies
q: how do towns know each other's strength
entries.answer: At war a town stands on a war footing: the militia drills, the larder is kept for a siege, bandages and arrows are made, and the war stores fill (Wanted orders). Scouts go out to read the enemy's strength; their reports age, and a quest may ask you to scout a rival and bring back a spy's report.

entries.title: Vassal towns, tribute and ruins
q: what happens to the losing town
entries.answer: A war ends at the table: terms are agreed (a border, tribute, a trade deal, satisfaction), and a beaten town may become a vassal paying tribute. After a war come prisoners, ruins where things burned, and outlaws; the War page keeps the record.
